subjects.description: RFC-BPR-0017 stays Deferred, BPR-0312 stays unresolved, and every implementation card (BPR-0300 through BPR-0317) stays dependency-blocked. The device-authorization flow (RFC-BPR-0016, shipped on macOS since BPR-0318) is the answer to reading a pull request without a stored token, as the RFC itself recommends when the rate budget is not workable.

detail_sections.heading: Measured facts (docs/verification/reviews/rfc0017-anonymous-probe-v001)
items: Unauthenticated REST core budget: x-ratelimit-limit 60 per hour per source address, shared by every client behind that address; opening one pull request costs several requests.
A conditional GET answered 304 Not Modified consumed one core unit (used 3 -> 4), so refresh is not exempt.
GraphQL refuses anonymous callers with 403 and x-ratelimit-limit 0, so the workbench's review-thread selection has no anonymous route.
REST pull-request review comments answered 200 anonymously (per_page=1 course), so source-anchored comments could be recovered through a new read operation nobody has carded.
A private or missing repository answers 404, so the mode cannot distinguish absent from private.
GHES in private mode rejects all unauthenticated access; the mode would be GitHub.com-only.

subjects.description: Accept the measured limits and authorize the RFC-BPR-0017 implementation cards. Accept only with a note that gives the four things the approval must define: the public-preview name, how the 60-per-hour shared limit and the missing review threads and triage are presented, the sign-in handoff to the device flow, and the supported-platform policy (GitHub.com only). BPR-0312 validates that positive decision next.

detail_sections.heading: Required in the accepting note
items: Exact public-preview naming.
Limit presentation: the shared 60-per-hour budget, the 304 cost, and the absent review threads and triage.

Supported-platform policy: GitHub.com public repositories only; every GHES profile stays unavailable.
